identity.name: MARATHON NXTGEN REALT LTD
identity.industry: Real Estate / Mumbai Suburban Integrated Townships & Commercial Redevelopment

summary.oneLiner: Marathon delivered record H1 PAT of INR128cr (+47% YoY) driven by strong sales velocity in Futurex, Monte South, and Nexzone, with a robust launch pipeline and QIP-funded capital to accelerate monetization of its 400+ acre land bank across high-growth Mumbai micro-markets.

one-line thesis: Marathon delivered record H1 PAT of INR128cr (+47% YoY) driven by strong sales velocity in Futurex, Monte South, and Nexzone, with a robust launch pipeline and QIP-funded capital to accelerate monetization of its 400+ acre land bank across high-growth Mumbai micro-markets.
financial scorecard: revenue: INR430cr (H1 FY26, +17% YoY); EBITDA/margin: not disclosed; PAT (rptd): INR128cr (H1 FY26, +47% YoY); PAT (normalized): same; order book: INR349cr (H1 bookings); net debt: net debt-free
guidance: revenue growth: implied 25-30% YoY for FY26 based on H1 performance; margin: maintained via premium mix and FSI trading; order inflow: INR166cr (Q2), pipeline includes Nirvana Collection (INR600cr GDV), Neohomes Bandu (INR370cr GDV), Monte South Commercial (INR3400cr GDV); capex/commissioning: focused on self-development; no new capex guidance beyond existing projects
order book & pipeline: INR349cr (H1 FY26 bookings); major contributors: Futurex (commercial), Monte South (residential/commercial), Nexzone (residential)
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: Nexzone (Panvel, INR600cr GDV Phase 3), Neohomes (Bhandup, INR370cr GDV), Monte South (Bhandup, part OC for Tower B); Commercial: Futurex (strong tenant expansion), Monte South Commercial (JV with Adani, 7.5L sq.ft, INR3400cr GDV); Land Bank: 400+ acres across Bhandup (130ac), Panvel (205ac), Dombivli (80ac+)
growth verticals / optionality: JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai using QIP funds; FSI trading to third-party builders; large-scale township development in Panvel and Dombivli; potential demerger of commercial assets post-stabilization
margins & cost dynamics: Margins improving via premium mix (Monte South, Futurex), FSI trading (Bhandup), and in-house execution; cost discipline maintained; no inflationary pressure cited; rental yields rising in commercial assets
capex / expansion: Capex focused on self-development of existing land bank; no new land acquisition capex; QIP proceeds (INR900cr) allocated to project execution, slum clearance, and JDA/JV opportunities
capital allocation: Prioritized: 1) project execution (Monte South Tower C, Nexzone Phase 3); 2) JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai; 3) FSI trading; 4) slum clearance infrastructure; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Slum clearance delays in Bhandup; environmental clearances for forest-adjacent plots; execution risk in large-scale township development; regulatory delays in Panvel 3.0 infrastructure rollout
management quality / tone: Highly confident and bullish; emphasized execution discipline, land bank value, infrastructure tailwinds (bullet train, airport, freeways), and QIP-funded acceleration; repeated use of 'strong', 'phenomenal', 'bright future'
non-obvious takeaways: Marathon is quietly becoming a key enabler of Mumbai's slum rehabilitation via SRA cluster plans — leveraging its 50+ acre holdings to become a preferred partner for municipal redevelopment, not just a developer

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
